text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.4% today as oil prices weakened and the broader refining trade showed signs of cooling. US crude dropped to $89.53 per barrel, and headlines emphasized that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding"—a direct headwind for energy majors that have benefited from historically strong refining margins. The stock has now surrendered most of its recent gains, sliding from $140.52 two weeks ago.

Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East (Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries, Iranian drone incidents) briefly supported oil prices earlier in the week, but those haven't been enough to offset the broader shift in market sentiment away from energy stocks. With climate negotiations also failing to endorse fossil fuels at COP31, the near-term tailwinds that pushed energy stocks higher are fading.
